The petitioners of MVC No.4777/2023 and 4743/2023 have filed these petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1989 seeking compensation for the death of Ghouse Basha Nazeer @ Gouse Basha and Imthiyas S. @ Imthiyas Shaik Peer respectively in the road traffic accident occurred on 01.07.2023.
 2.
The petitioners of MVC No.4777/2023 have filed application to club MVC No.4743/2023 with it.
The said application came to be allowed on the ground that the respondents in both the cases are one and the same and the injuries caused from the same accident.
Hence, both these cases are clubbed together to lead common evidence.
3. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follow:-

On 01.07.2023 at about 2.30 a.m. when the deceased Ghouse Basha Nazeer and Imthiyaz along with others were traveling in  SCCH-08 5 MVC No.4777/23 c/w. 4743/23 Mahindra Xylo Car bearing Reg. No.TN-91-6507 driven by one Shamiullah, near Kallugopahalli village, on Bengaluru - Mysore NH-275 Road, Bidadi Hobli, Ramanagara, at that time, without anticipating the distance of the Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AA- 5682 which was going ahead of the Car, the said car driver went at high speed and dashed to rear side of the lorry, caused the accident, due to which he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

4. It is contended that, immediately after the accident,
deceased were shifted to Rajarajeshwari Medical College hospital,
wherein after post-mortem the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.
 5.

It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-91-6507.

The police intimation given by the Super Specialty hospital on 01.07.2023 stating history of injury as RTA while traveling in car,
its driver hit to the lorry.
The manner and involvement of the offending car is not disputed by the respondent No.4.
The I.M.V report shows the damages caused to the car bearing Reg. No.TN- 91-6507 and lorry Reg No.KA-01-C-9430 and no explanation given by the respondents for the damages caused to car and lorry.
Therefore, there is no reason to distrust the evidence of the petitioners in this regard.
As per the first information report the police have registered case against the driver of the car, after investigation of the case the Police have registered the case against the driver car.
As per the Charge sheet driver car was offender in the alleged accident.

The charge sheet and sketch discloses that the driver of the Mahindra Xylo Car without anticipating the distance of the Lorry which was going ahead of the Car, by driving it in negligent manner and dashed to the rear side of the lorry.

If at all the driver of the Mahindra Xylo Car would have taken precautionary measures and kept distance with the front vehicle and driven the vehicle in a slow manner and he could have avoided the accident.
But the driver of car was unable apply brake since he was driving his vehicle at a high speed and dashed to Lorry.
Charge sheet further discloses that the accident has occurred due to the negligence of Car driver.

The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent has argued that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the car,
because driver of the car touched the lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51- AA-5682, since lorry without indication or signal suddenly stopped which is not proper and fair in the eyes of law and negligence is on the part of the driver of the lorry.

It is also argued that though police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the car, but there are decisions with respect to filing of charge sheet wherein investigation officer should be honest and he should speak through the materials as is held in MFA 2921/2012 of Ho'nle High Court of Karnataka in Smt. 16. With regard to the arguments canvassed by the respondent No.2 counsel that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the car because driver of the car touched the lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AA-5682, since lorry without indication or signal suddenly stopped and negligence is on the part of the driver  SCCH-08 12 MVC No.4777/23 c/w. 4743/23 of the lorry and false charge sheet is filed against the driver of the car.

However petitioners in the petition itself have stated that the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the car,
the driver of the car without anticipating the distance of the lorry which was going ahead of the car, dashed to rear side of the lorry and the police have filed FIR against him and charge sheet is also filed against the driver of the car.
It has to be noted that the said charge sheet is not challenged by the driver of the car.

In view of the discussion made supra, I hold that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending Car bearing Reg. No. TN-91-6507 and at the same time there is no fault of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-01-C-9430.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 in both the cases in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: 19 . The petitioners have contended that the deceased was self employed and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not produced any document to show the income of the deceased.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence with regard to the income of the deceased, the court has to take into consideration the notional income.
Considering the work of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- per month.
20 . It is stated that the deceased was aged 41 years at the time of the accident.
The petitioners have produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P23 which shows the date of birth as 16.02.1982.
The accident was occurred on 01.07.2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 41 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '14'.
 21.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor  SCCH-08 14 MVC No.4777/23 c/w. 4743/23 accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of  the deceased and percentage for future prospects in  between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50  years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 41 years.
Therefore, in this case, 25% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.
If 25% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.20,000/- p.m.. (Rs.16,000/- + 4,000/- i.e. 25%).
The deceased died leaving behind 3 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case,
1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.13,334/- p.m.(Rs.20,000 - Rs.6,666 =
Rs.13,334/-).

22. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.13,334/- p.m.
and the multiplier '14' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.22,40,112/- (Rs.13,334 X 12 X 14).

Considering the above Najma vs Shameena Banju A R on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147145536/
10 facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.22,40,112/- under the head of loss of dependency.
